output.methodChoice: Evidence-ledger provenance check (vendor report vs system records), then competing-hypotheses comparison
output.brief:
The fall in incidents is not real. Tessaline's audit trail shows 37 cases reached Incident–Confirmed in September and 36 in October, in line with the old ~38 a month. 47 of those cases (23 and 24) were then moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring", which the report doesn't count. Each had an analyst's confirmation note. Every move was made 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the 4-hour SLA warning flag was raised. The moves came from a script on a Brackwater analyst jump host that polls for flagged cases and re-categorises them. The platform connector wrote no categories. So this looks deliberate rather than a software fault, though who ordered it is unproven. The "100% within SLA" figure and the 60k bonus rest on cases being removed from the metric. The Monitoring queue growth (40 to 96) fits this. I'm not certain about the 28 dropped detection rules; that is unchecked.

Do not cut the IR retainer or approve the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases, have the in-house team and Halvard verify containment on each, and remove category-edit rights from the integration role. Get Brackwater's written explanation before renewal. Hold off on invoicing service credits until the facts are settled.
